Recent analyses from Berkeley Earth, NOAA, and ECMWF show June and July 2026 ranking among the warmest months on record at approximately 1.5–1.56°C above the 1850–1900 baseline, with August projections around 1.6°C amid elevated sea surface temperatures and positive anomalies in the equatorial Pacific. This positioning reflects trader consensus on the lagged global response to El Niño and sustained energy imbalance, though an unusually rapid weakening of the event or stronger La Niña transition could modestly lower outcomes.
